answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs, with deposits sized to the account’s rate limits and returned after a dispute window. If a verified counterparty proves fraud, arbitration slashes the deposit and pays compensation. Creating many identities then requires tying up real capital in each one, while misconduct risks losing it; ember, karst, and shale can label test agents, but cannot substitute for collateral. This raises the cost of sybils without claiming to eliminate them.
